nodes.name: Urea-assisted NiFe-LDH formation
nodes.procedure: During hydrolysis reactions, the released Feᴵᴵ species from Fe-soc-MOF coprecipitated with Niᴵᴵ and OH⁻ ions to form layered FeNi-LDH on the surface of Fe-soc-MOF under urea assisted hydrolysis process. After reacting 4h the optimized MOF/LDH-4h heterostructure was prepared.

nodes.name: Targeted anchoring and spontaneous reduction
nodes.procedure: When K₂PtCl₄ was added into the MOF/LDH-4h dispersion, Ptᴵᴵ were targeted-anchored and stabilized in the MOF/LDH heterostructure monodisperse. Within the reaction time, Ptᴵᴵ was exchanged with the Feᴵᴵ in the MOF/LDH heterostructure. At the same time, due to the more favorable thermodynamic process, Ptᴵᴵ specie could be spontaneous-reduced to low-valence Pt. After reducing for 6h, monodispersed Pt sites supported on NiFe-LDH (named Pt@LDH-4h) were prepared.

nodes.source_text: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curve of Pt@LDH-4h displayed the excellent catalytic activity, that with low HER overpotential of 58.7 mV at 10 mA cm⁻², much better than MOF/LDH-4h (η₁₀ = 519.7 mV) and Fe-soc-MOF (η₁₀ = 591.7 mV)... Pt@LDH-4h exhibited a Tafel slope of 43.6 mV dec⁻¹... Pt@LDH-4h exhibited much higher C_dl (2.4 mF cm⁻²), and the corresponding ECSA was 57.5 cm⁻²... Specific activities normalized by BET surface areas display that Pt@LDH-4h (0.25 mA cm⁻²) shows much higher activity... Pt@LDH-4h showed excellent durability, that a slight fluctuation could be observed at the current density of 100 mA cm⁻² after 24 h i-t test.

Pt@LDH-4h possessed much lower overpotentials (η₁₀ = 239 mV)... The excellent OER activity of Pt@LDH-4h was also confirmed by its smaller Tafel slope (28.4 mV dec⁻¹)... Pt@LDH-4h reveals the largest C_dl and ECSA value of 2.3 mF cm⁻² and 57.5 cm²... After chronopotentiometry test for 24 h at 100 mA cm⁻²... there almost have no change in current density.

nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images of Pt@LDH-4h showed the uniform-blossom nanosheets morphology (Figure 2b,c and Figure S8, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt@LDH-4h shows ultra-thin nanosheets with thickness of about 2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: AFM image of Pt@LDH-4h showed ultra-thin nanosheets with the thickness of about 2 nm (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt@LDH-4h shows ultra-thin blossom-like nanosheets morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images further confirmed the ultra-thin blossom-like nanosheets morphology (Figure 2e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows abundant dispersive bright spots representing Pt metal sites on Pt@LDH-4h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) of Pt@LDH-4h (Figure 2g) showed the abundant dispersive bright spots, representing the Pt metal sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt sites show lattice fringes of 0.22 nm corresponding to Pt (111) plane; LDH substrate shows 0.15 nm corresponding to (110) facet of NiFe-LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringes of Pt specie possessed 0.22 nm with an angle of 80°, assigning to the Pt (111) plane (Figure 2i). HR-TEM image displayed the lattice spacing of LDH substrate is 0.15 nm (Figure 2i), corresponding to the (110) facet of NiFe-LDHs.
Determined by the inductively coupled plasma (ICP), the optimized Pt@LDH-4h possessed the ultra-low precious metal content, which loaded about 5.5 wt% Pt (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt@LDH-4h exhibits specific surface area of 105 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe-soc-MOF, MOF/LDH-4h and Pt@LDH-4h exhibited the specific surface areas of 848, 301, and 105 m²g⁻¹, respectively (Figure S10, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f spectrum of Pt@LDH-4h similar with Pt foil confirming low valence Pt; Ni 2p positive shift of 0.2 eV from 885.5 to 885.7 eV indicating electron transfer to Pt; increasing FeIII content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt 4f spectrum of Pt@LDH-4h was similar with Pt foil (Figure 3a), confirming successful formation of low valence Pt... Compared with MOF/LDH-4h, the Ni 2p spectrum of Pt@LDH-4h had a positive shift of about 0.2 eV from 885.5 to 885.7 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES: Pt@LDH-4h absorption edge between Pt foil and PtO2, average Pt valence +0.96; Fe K-edge pre-edge peak close to Fe2O3 confirming Fe3+ valence; Ni K-edge close to NiO indicating Ni2+ valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Normalized Pt L3-edge XANES spectra exhibited that the absorption edge of Pt@LDH-4h was located between Pt foil and PtO2... Fe K-edge XANES spectra showed that the pre-edge peak of Pt@LDH-4h was close to the Fe2O3 reference... Ni K-edge XANES spectra revealed that the absorption threshold for Pt@LDH-4h was close to that of NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt@LDH-4h shows Pt-O at 1.99 Å (CN=2.6), Pt-M at 2.73 Å (CN=3.8); confirms single Pt atoms and NPs with unsaturated coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EXAFS fitting of Pt@LDH-4h sample (Figure 3d and Table S2, Supporting Information) gave the average coordination number (CN) of 2.6 and 3.8 for Pt-O (1.99 Å) contribution and Pt-M (2.73 Å) contribution.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt@LDH-4h shows Cdl = 2.4 mF/cm² corresponding to ECSA = 57.5 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the Fe-soc-MOF (1.2 mFcm⁻²) and MOF/LDH-4h (1.6 mFcm⁻²), Pt@LDH-4h exhibited much higher Cdl (2.4 mFcm⁻²), and the corresponding ECSA was 57.5 cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt@LDH-4h shows greatest drop in impedance in low-frequency regime indicating faster charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt@LDH-4h showed the greatest drop degree of impedance in the low-frequency regime, suggesting faster charge transfer and OH⁻ adsorption.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows successful Pt introduction and Pt/Fe ion substitution in Pt@LDH-4h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping images of Pt@LDH-4h illustrated the successful introduction of Pt and ions substitution between Pt and Fe (Figure 2j).
